instruction: Center-align the title 'H2O—Soak up the Science' in the document.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully selected the '2' character in 'H2O' title and applied subscript formatting via Format > Text > Subscript menu, then saved the document. Completed in 11 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select specific characters in LibreOffice Writer, navigate Format menu, apply text formatting (subscript), save documents
metadata.task_rationale: The model demonstrated paragraph-level formatting skills. This variation tests changing paragraph alignment to center, requiring cursor placement in the title and alignment change via toolbar or menu.
metadata.explanation: Task requires placing cursor in the title and center-aligning it. Getter reads the docx file and checks the alignment property of the title paragraph (index 1). Metric compares actual alignment string to expected 'center'.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the docx file via python-docx and extracts the alignment property of the title paragraph, mapping WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH enum to human-readable strings.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses expected.get('expected_alignment') since expected IS the rules dict {'expected_alignment': 'center'}.
Postconfig properly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring persisted state.
Complete coverage: instruction only requires center-alignment of the title, and the evaluator checks exactly that.

Minor concern: getter hardcodes doc.paragraphs[1] as the title without verifying the paragraph text contains 'H2O—Soak up the Science'. If the document structure differs, it could check the wrong paragraph.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a text verification step in the getter to confirm that doc.paragraphs[1].text contains 'H2O' before checking alignment, to guard against unexpected document structure.
